content:
# Disagreement Log — Gospel of Philip, Chapter 1 (GPH 001)

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Translators:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, pp. 51-86 | Coptic
**Total Disagreements:** 41

---

## Format
Each entry: **Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | Resolution**

---

**1. v. 1 — "proselyte" vs. "convert"**
- EMET: "proselyte" (Greek loan-word preserved as technical term)
- LOGOS: "proselyte" (preserves the technical religious category)
- PNEUMA: "convert" (renders the meaning accessibly)
- **Resolution:** "proselyte" — the word is already a naturalized English religious term and carries the precise meaning of the Coptic *prosēlytos*.

---

**2. v. 2 — "estate" vs. "wealth" vs. "world"**
- EMET: "estate" (*ousia* — technical term for property/being)
- LOGOS: "estate"
- PNEUMA: "whole world" (interpretive expansion)
- **Resolution:** "estate" — closer to *ousia* which denotes property/substance, not a general expanse.

---

**3. v. 5 — "Gentile" vs. "pagan"**
- EMET: "Gentile" (*ethnikos*)
- LOGOS: "Gentile"
- PNEUMA: "pagan"
- **Resolution:** "Gentile" — *ethnikos* means one of the nations; "pagan" imports a later pejorative connotation not present in the Coptic.

---

**4. v. 6 — tense and sequence of creation events**
- EMET: "the world was created, cities were established, the dead were buried" (past passive)
- LOGOS: "the world has been created, cities have been established" (perfect aspect)
- PNEUMA: "the world was created, cities were built, and the dead were laid to rest"
- **Resolution:** Simple past — the text presents these as accomplished events following Christ's coming.

---

**5. v. 8 — meaning of the winter/summer allegory**
- EMET: Renders literally; note explains "aeon" = eschatological age
- LOGOS: Preserves "aeon" with light contextual framing
- PNEUMA: Interprets "summer" as "the coming age" (supplies meaning in text)
- **Resolution:** Preserve "aeon" without gloss in the text; contextual note explains. PNEUMA's gloss is appropriate for dynamic register only.

---

**6. v. 10 — "ransom," "save," "redeem" as three distinct acts**
- EMET: "ransom / save / redeem" — three distinct verbs preserved
- LOGOS: Same three verbs
- PNEUMA: "ransom / rescue / set free" — varying the verbs for rhythmic variety
- **Resolution:** The Coptic uses three distinct verbs (*nahm / sohe / tbbe*); EMET/LOGOS preserve the distinction. PNEUMA's variation is acceptable in dynamic register but the consensus preserves three distinct terms.

---

**7. v. 11 — "soul" (*psychē*) vs. "life"**
- EMET: "laid down his soul" (*psychē*)
- LOGOS: "laid down his life" (idiomatic)
- PNEUMA: "laid down his life"
- **Resolution:** "life" — the idiomatic English "lay down one's life" captures the intended meaning; "soul" sounds unnatural in this context and may mislead.

---

**8. v. 12 — "brothers of one another" — gendered language**
- EMET: "brothers" (*snēu* — masculine plural in Coptic)
- LOGOS: "brothers"
- PNEUMA: "brothers and sisters" (inclusive interpretation)
- **Resolution:** "brothers" — the Coptic *snēu* is grammatically masculine. A literal/formal rendering preserves the text; PNEUMA's expansion is interpretive.

---

**9. v. 13 — "deceptive" vs. "misleading" vs. "profoundly deceptive"**
- EMET: "very deceptive" (*referpłana* — "one who leads astray")
- LOGOS: "profoundly deceptive"
- PNEUMA: "deeply misleading"
- **Resolution:** "profoundly deceptive" — captures both the intensity and the active quality of the Coptic participial form.

---

**10. v. 13 — what "God" as a name refers to**
- EMET: "does not perceive what is real, but perceives what is not real"
- LOGOS: Same structure
- PNEUMA: "does not grasp the real thing — only an image of it" (adds "image")
- **Resolution:** "does not perceive the real but only the unreal" — PNEUMA's addition of "image" goes beyond the text at this point; the image motif appears elsewhere.

---

**11. v. 14 — "uttered" vs. "spoken" vs. "said aloud"**
- EMET: "not uttered"
- LOGOS: "not uttered"
- PNEUMA: "never spoken aloud"
- **Resolution:** "not uttered" — precise and preserves the formal register appropriate to a saying about a sacred name.

---

**12. v. 16 — "archons" — transliterate or translate**
- EMET: "archons" (preserved as technical term with note)
- LOGOS: "archons" (preserved with context)
- PNEUMA: "the archons" (preserved — PNEUMA agrees on this term)
- **Resolution:** "archons" — all three translators agree. Term is standard in Valentinian studies and Nag Hammadi scholarship.

---

**13. v. 18 — "dissolve" vs. "are absorbed into"**
- EMET: "dissolve together with the things dyed in them" (*bol ebol*)
- LOGOS: "dissolve together"
- PNEUMA: "dissolve into the things they dye"
- **Resolution:** "dissolve together with the things dyed in them" — the Coptic *bol ebol* implies a mutual dissolution; the dye and the dyed thing become one.

---

**14. v. 19 — "perceive" vs. "see" vs. "grasp"**
- EMET: "perceive" (*nau* — to see/perceive)
- LOGOS: "perceive"
- PNEUMA: "grasp/see" (varying)
- **Resolution:** "perceive" consistently — *nau* in the Coptic means to see, but in this philosophical context carries the weight of intellectual/spiritual perception.

---

**15. v. 21 — "perfect man" (*teleios*) — capital or lower case**
- EMET: "the perfect man" (lower case, Coptic adjective)
- LOGOS: "the perfect man"
- PNEUMA: "the complete human" (gender-neutral, avoids "perfect")
- **Resolution:** "the perfect man" — *teleios* is a Valentinian technical term meaning the initiated/spiritually complete person; "man" is appropriate given the Adamic typology in context. PNEUMA's "complete human" is acceptable but loses the technical resonance.

---

**16. v. 22 — "secretly" vs. "in secret" vs. "behind the scenes"**
- EMET: "in secret" (*hn oumntkryfaios*)
- LOGOS: "secretly"
- PNEUMA: "working behind the scenes" (interpretive paraphrase)
- **Resolution:** "secretly" — concise and accurate. PNEUMA's paraphrase adds interpretive color not in the text.

---

**17. v. 24 — "conceived" vs. "impregnated" vs. "became pregnant"**
- EMET: "impregnated by the Holy Spirit" (direct)
- LOGOS: "conceived by the Holy Spirit"
- PNEUMA: "became pregnant by the Holy Spirit"
- **Resolution:** "conceived by the Holy Spirit" — standard rendering; "impregnated" (EMET) is accurate but blunter; "became pregnant" (PNEUMA) is clearer for modern readers. Consensus: "conceived."

---

**18. v. 24 — "anathema" — preserve or translate**
- EMET: "anathema" (preserved)
- LOGOS: "anathema" (preserved as a recognizable term)
- PNEUMA: "a scandal" (dynamic rendering)
- **Resolution:** "anathema" — the Greek loan-word appears in the Coptic; it is recognizable in English and preserves the precise theological register.

---

**19. v. 27 — "hidden name" / "revealed name" — the nature of "Jesus"**
- EMET: "Jesus is a hidden name; Christ is a revealed name" — with note on linguistic argument
- LOGOS: Same
- PNEUMA: Same — all three agree on this distinction
- **Resolution:** Unanimous. "Jesus" as hidden name and "Christ" as revealed name is the text's own claim; all translations reflect it faithfully.

---

**20. v. 28 — hierarchy of sacraments**
- EMET: "the holy" / "holy of holies" / "holy of holies" — noting the text's apparent repetition
- LOGOS: Renders baptism = "the holy"; redemption = "the holy of holies"; bridal chamber = holiest of all (disambiguating)
- PNEUMA: "highest" / "the innermost sanctum" (interpretive)
- **Resolution:** LOGOS rendering adopted: baptism = "the holy," redemption = "the holy of holies," bridal chamber = "holiest of all / the innermost." The text's hierarchy is preserved without flattening the distinctions.

---

**21. v. 34 — "by stealth" vs. "in disguise" vs. "secretly"**
- EMET: "by stealth" (*mnteibt*)
- LOGOS: "by stealth"
- PNEUMA: "not as he truly was" (paraphrases the stealth idea away)
- **Resolution:** "by stealth" — the Coptic term implies craftiness/cunning in approach, not merely hiddenness.

---

**22. v. 35 — "prayer of thanksgiving" vs. "eucharistic prayer"**
- EMET: "prayer of thanksgiving" (*eucharistia*)
- LOGOS: "eucharistic prayer"
- PNEUMA: "prayer of thanksgiving"
- **Resolution:** "prayer of thanksgiving" — more transparent to the Greek loan-word's meaning; "eucharistic prayer" is a later liturgical technical term that may import anachronistic connotations.

---

**23. v. 40 — "type" vs. "sign" vs. "image"**
- EMET: "type" (*typos*)
- LOGOS: "type"
- PNEUMA: "sign" (dynamic equivalent)
- **Resolution:** "type" — *typos* is a specific hermeneutical-theological term used throughout this text; it should be preserved consistently. PNEUMA's "sign" loses the typological register.

---

**24. v. 42 — "sires" / "begets" / "brings forth" — generative verbs**
- EMET: "sires / begets / brings forth" (three distinct verbs matching species)
- LOGOS: "sires / begets / brings forth"
- PNEUMA: "born of / begets / brings forth"
- **Resolution:** EMET/LOGOS: "sires" for horse, "begets" for man, "brings forth" for god — the variation appropriately reflects the different subjects.

---

**25. v. 43 — "in error" vs. "wrong" vs. "mistaken"**
- EMET: "in error" (*rpłana*)
- LOGOS: "in error"
- PNEUMA: "wrong"
- **Resolution:** "in error" — the Coptic *rpłana* derives from Greek *planē* (wandering/error), a term with specific theological weight in early Christian contexts.

---

**26. v. 44 — "offspring" vs. "flesh and blood" (PNEUMA's addition)**
- EMET: "his offspring" (*speima*)
- LOGOS: "his own offspring"
- PNEUMA: "His own flesh and blood" (interpretive addition not in text)
- **Resolution:** "his offspring" — PNEUMA adds "flesh and blood" which is not in the Coptic *speima* (seed/offspring). This is a significant departure.

---

**27. v. 45 — "corpse-eater" vs. "feeds on corpses"**
- EMET: "a corpse-eater" (*ourefouom nbake* — participial compound)
- LOGOS: "a corpse-eater"
- PNEUMA: "feeds on corpses"
- **Resolution:** "a corpse-eater" — the Coptic forms a compound noun; rendering it as a compound noun in English preserves the rhetorical impact.

---

**28. v. 49 — "Pharisath" etymology — how to handle**
- EMET: Presents as the text's claim with a note questioning philological validity
- LOGOS: Presents as the text's claim without endorsement
- PNEUMA: Presents as the text's claim; notes it as "creative etymology"
- **Resolution:** All translators present the etymology as the text's own assertion. Notes in EMET and PNEUMA signal uncertainty; SOPHIA's council note addresses this.

---

**29. v. 51 / v. 119 — the lacuna in the Mary Magdalene passage**
- EMET: "used to kiss her often on the [...]" — lacuna preserved
- LOGOS: "used to kiss her often on the [...]" — lacuna preserved
- PNEUMA: "used to kiss her often on the [...]" — lacuna preserved
- **Resolution:** Unanimous — the lacuna is preserved. No translation supplies the missing word. This is a firm editorial rule.

---

**30. v. 51 — "companion" (*koinonos*) — range of meaning**
- EMET: "companion" (*koinonos* — partner, consort, companion)
- LOGOS: "companion"
- PNEUMA: "companion"
- **Resolution:** "companion" — *koinonos* means one who shares, a partner; all translators agree. Stronger translations ("consort," "spouse") exceed what the text warrants without further context.

---

**31. v. 56 — listing of five sacraments**
- EMET: "a baptism and a chrism and a Eucharist and a redemption and a bridal chamber" (with Coptic terms)
- LOGOS: "a baptism, a chrism, a Eucharist, a redemption, and a bridal chamber"
- PNEUMA: "a baptism, a chrism, a Eucharist, a redemption, a bridal chamber"
- **Resolution:** Unanimous on terms. The five sacraments are named identically across all three translations.

---

**32. v. 57 — "I came to make... like..." — authorship of the saying**
- EMET: Brackets the saying as reported speech: "[He said:]"
- LOGOS: Introduces without bracket
- PNEUMA: Introduces as direct quotation
- **Resolution:** "[He said:]" — EMET's bracketing is appropriate since the subject of the saying is implied, not stated. Consistent with scholarly practice.

---

**33. v. 61 — Eve in Adam — the separation and reunion**
- EMET: "When Eve was still in Adam" (literal spatial metaphor)
- LOGOS: "When Eve was still within Adam" (same)
- PNEUMA: "When Eve was still inside Adam" (same)
- **Resolution:** "When Eve was still within Adam" — all three agree on the essential reading; minor stylistic variation is resolved by the LOGOS rendering.

---

**34. v. 64 — "rebirth" vs. "regeneration" (*palingenesia*)**
- EMET: "rebirth" (*palingenesia*)
- LOGOS: "rebirth"
- PNEUMA: "rebirth"
- **Resolution:** Unanimous. "Rebirth" is the agreed rendering of *palingenesia*.

---

**35. v. 64 — "restoration" vs. "apokatastasis"**
- EMET: "restoration" (*apokatastasis*) with note on Origenist background
- LOGOS: "restoration"
- PNEUMA: "restoration"
- **Resolution:** "restoration" — all agree; the term is rendered into English rather than transliterated, with scholarly notes in EMET providing the Greek technical term.

---

**36. v. 77 — "Word" (*Logos*) — capitalize or not**
- EMET: "Logos" (preserved in Greek form, capitalized)
- LOGOS: "Word" (capitalized)
- PNEUMA: "Word" (capitalized)
- **Resolution:** "Word" — the Coptic uses *logos* as a Greek loan-word; rendering as "Word" is standard English convention for this term in theological contexts (cf. John 1:1).

---

**37. v. 88 — "repair" vs. "rectify" vs. "undo"**
- EMET: "repair" (*sops*)
- LOGOS: "rectify"
- PNEUMA: "repair"
- **Resolution:** "repair" — the Coptic *sops* means to set right/repair; "rectify" (LOGOS) is slightly more formal but acceptable. Consensus: "repair" as more vivid.

---

**38. v. 93 — "axe" saying — attribution**
- EMET: Attributes to "the Logos" (the Word)
- LOGOS: "the Word says"
- PNEUMA: Attributes to "the Word"
- **Resolution:** "the Word says" — the text attributes this saying (cf. Matt. 3:10 / Luke 3:9) to the Logos, not to a named prophet; all translations reflect this.

---

**39. v. 107 — "puffs up" vs. "lifts up" vs. "makes arrogant"**
- EMET: "merely puffs up their hearts" (*ĵose ehra*i — to exalt/raise)
- LOGOS: "merely lifts up their hearts"
- PNEUMA: "only swells their hearts"
- **Resolution:** "merely lifts up their hearts" — the Coptic verb *ĵose* means to be/make high/exalted; PNEUMA's "swells" imports a negative connotation slightly beyond the text; LOGOS is more literal.

---

**40. v. 110 — "bad smell" vs. "unpleasant odor" vs. "foul smell"**
- EMET: "bad smell" (*hmou*)
- LOGOS: "unpleasant smell"
- PNEUMA: "bad smell"
- **Resolution:** "bad smell" — direct and appropriate. The Coptic *hmou* is simply "smell/odor" with the context implying its unpleasantness; "bad smell" is the most natural English rendering.

---

**41. v. 124 — "defiled women" vs. "impure women" vs. "women who have been made unclean"**
- EMET: "defiled women" (*tako* — corruption/defilement)
- LOGOS: "defiled women"
- PNEUMA: "women who have been defiled"
- **Resolution:** "defiled women" — concise rendering of *tako*; the passive construction of PNEUMA is equally valid but wordier. EMET/LOGOS preferred.

---

## Summary Statistics
- **Total disagreements logged:** 41
- **Unanimous resolutions:** 9 (vv. 19 PNEUMA addition, v. 27, v. 29/119 lacuna, v. 30/koinonos, v. 56 sacraments, v. 61, v. 64/rebirth, v. 64/restoration, v. 93)
- **EMET/LOGOS vs. PNEUMA:** 18 cases (PNEUMA's dynamic register introduces the most variation)
- **LOGOS adopted in consensus:** 7 cases
- **EMET adopted in consensus:** 10 cases
- **Novel consensus rendering:** 6 cases

## Key Ruling: The Mary Magdalene Lacuna
All three translators independently preserved the manuscript lacuna at v. 51 / v. 119 without supplying the missing word. This is confirmed as project-wide policy for this text: **the lacuna is never filled**. Scholarly notes may discuss the possibilities; the translation does not.

## Key Ruling: Technical Terms
The following terms are preserved in all translations without substitution:
- **archons** (not "rulers" or "powers")
- **bridal chamber** (not "wedding chamber" or "inner room")
- **chrism** (not "anointing oil")
- **Eucharist** (not "communion" or "thanksgiving meal")
- **Logos/Word** (capitalized)
- **aeon** (not "age" or "eternity" alone)
- **apokatastasis → restoration** (rendered, not transliterated)
- **nymphon → bridal chamber** (rendered)
- **teleios → perfect** (not "complete" or "mature")

---
